title: An approve without a schedule drops the review's attached notes
instrument: next-server test: a `step` packet-review approve with a 1-note plan -> the kept verdict's note carries the note (0 of 1 today) and the step applier's behaviour for a noted keep is unchanged
evidence: packages/ui/src/components/review/PacketReview.tsx:117-121 (`if (schedule === null) return { verdict: "keep", reasons: [] }` under the comment 'The attached notes ride with the approve'); packages/domain/src/source.ts:103 step noteMax NOTE_LONG, modes packet-review
body:
## Summary
keepVerdict only attaches the edit-plan notes when the source schedules; a step review's approve loses them.

## Description
The comment above keepVerdict promises the attached notes ride with the approve (prototype decide({notes})). With schedule === null (step, dojo) the note is omitted entirely, though step accepts 2000 chars. Dojo's noteMax is 0, so the fix must keep it note-less.

## Flow
- attach a note on a step packet review
- press A
- the kept verdict carries no note

## Expected impact
The operator's approve-time notes reach the step record. Could break: a step applier that treats any keep note as a directive.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the stated promise holds for every source
Before: 0 of 1 noted step approves carry the note
After: 1 of 1 (predicted)
Method: simulation - the applier's reading of a keep note is in lib/decision/v1, outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none

title: PacketReview scrolls the window to its first section on mount
instrument: live kit spec: load /kit, assert window.scrollY === 0 after hydration (today: jumps to the PacketReview specimen); fix scopes the query to the component's own root and skips the mount run
evidence: packages/ui/src/components/review/PacketReview.tsx:79-81 (useEffect on [focus] runs on mount: document.querySelector('[data-sec="0"]').scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'})); app/(studio)/kit/BoardKit.tsx:185 renders it mid-page with keys={false}
body:
## Summary
The focus-scroll effect fires on mount and queries the whole document, so /kit jumps to the PacketReview specimen.

## Description
scrollIntoView({block:'nearest'}) on an off-screen element scrolls the window. The effect runs once on mount with focus 0 and is not limited to keys={true} or to this component's own sections.

## Flow
- open /kit
- PacketReview mounts
- the page scrolls to its section 0

## Expected impact
Kit opens at its top. Could break: the Board loses its initial scroll-to-section (harmless, section 0 is already the top).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - no unrequested scroll
Before: 1 jump on /kit load (walked)
After: 0
Method: simulation - needs a browser; dev servers and test:live are out of this round
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The review keymap says 'approve → calendar' on reviews that schedule nothing
instrument: keycaps markup test: Keycaps mode board.review rendered with facts without 'calendar' shows 'approve' (today 'approve → calendar'); with the fact, the arrow
evidence: packages/ui/src/keymap/bindings.ts:90 `does: "approve → calendar"` for every board.review; packages/ui/src/components/review/PacketReview.tsx:161 button reads 'Approve' when schedule === null (dojo, step)
body:
## Summary
The Keycaps legend promises a calendar slot on a dojo or step review, where the button itself says only Approve.

## Description
bindings.ts names one approve row for the whole mode. PacketReview already passes facts (['draft']); a 'calendar' fact, set when scheduleChannels(source) is non-empty, can choose between two rows.

## Flow
- open a step packet review
- read the key legend: 'A approve → calendar'
- the button reads 'Approve'; nothing is scheduled

## Expected impact
The legend and the button agree. Could break: keymap tests that pin the row count.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - copy states only what happens
Before: 2 of 3 packet-review sources show a false '→ calendar'
After: 0 of 3
Method: simulation - bindings.ts is the keymap's, outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none

title: The packet review's two columns have no narrow layout
instrument: cx-capture board (packet review) at --width 390: article column width before vs after a max-width breakpoint that stacks .side under .pageWrap
evidence: packages/ui/src/components/review/Review.module.css:6 `.review{grid-template-columns:minmax(0,1fr) var(--w-desk-side)}` with no @media; siblings Part.module.css, Plan.module.css, Receipt.module.css carry max-width breakpoints
body:
## Summary
At phone width the side panel keeps its fixed width and squeezes the article column.

## Description
The grid has no breakpoint while other desks stack at narrow widths. Whether the Board is a mobile route is the operator's call; the capture decides the figure.

## Flow
- open a packet review at 390 px
- the article column is what is left after --w-desk-side

## Expected impact
Readable review on a phone. Could break: nothing on desktop.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the article is readable at 390 px
Before: not captured (no dev server this round)
After: stacked columns (predicted)
Method: simulation - capture needs a dev server
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none

title: pack's every-interval track scan is quadratic in a track's bars
body: Before: pack + seatLabels over LEDGER_CAP 1000 bars = 3.00 ms per layout (24h), 1.62 ms (week); 52 ms only at 5000 one-minute bars, which the ledger cap never serves. After 3945ca8e the pass is off the scroll path. Rewriting the packer buys under 3 ms per data change: rejected.
